items.t: Asthma: regular treatment where an ICS/LABA combination is appropriate (not controlled on ICS plus as-needed SABA, or already controlled on ICS and LABA). 125/5: adults and adolescents 12 years and over. 250/10: adults only.

src.q: is indicated in the regular treatment of asthma where the use of a combination product (an inhaled corticosteroid and a long-acting β2 agonist) is appropriate
Flutiform 125 microgram / 5 microgram inhaler is indicated in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and above.
Flutiform 250 microgram /10 microgram inhaler is indicated in adults only.

items.t: Not for COPD (no data; should not be used). Not for initial treatment of mild asthma. Do not add another LABA for any reason.

src.q: Flutiform inhaler should not be used in patients with COPD.
Flutiform inhaler is not intended for the initial treatment of mild asthma.
Patients using Flutiform inhaler should not use additional long-acting β2 agonists for any reason.

items.t: MHRA (asthma): always prescribe a LABA with an inhaled corticosteroid, and only when ICS alone does not control symptoms; do not start a LABA in rapidly deteriorating asthma; review regularly, lowest effective dose, stop if no benefit. (This product already contains an ICS.)

src.q: always prescribe LABA with concomitant ICS and only when ICS alone are not sufficient to control asthma symptoms
LABA should not be initiated in patients with rapidly deteriorating asthma
review LABA therapy regularly, prescribe the lowest effective dose, and stop if there is no benefit

items.t: SPS: generic prescribing of inhalers can lead to an unfamiliar device, which could affect use and adherence (no specific brand instruction for this pressurised inhaler).

src.q: Generic prescribing of inhalers can lead to people being given an unfamiliar device which could affect usage and adherence.

items.t: NICE (asthma): if possible, use the same type of device for preventer and reliever when more than one inhaler is needed.

src.q: If possible, prescribe the same type of device to deliver preventer and reliever treatments where more than one inhaler is needed.

items.t: 125/5 (adults and adolescents 12 years and over): two puffs twice daily, morning and evening. This is also the recommended starting dose for patients on medium to high ICS doses who clearly need two maintenance therapies.

src.q: Flutiform 125 microgram/5 microgram inhaler - two inhalations (puffs) twice daily normally taken in the morning and in the evening.
the recommended starting dose is two inhalations twice daily of Flutiform 125 microgram /5 microgram inhaler

items.t: 250/10 (adults only): two puffs twice daily, morning and evening, if asthma remains poorly controlled on lower strengths.

src.q: Flutiform 250 microgram/10 microgram inhaler - two inhalations (puffs) twice daily normally taken in the morning and in the evening.

items.t: Titrate to the lowest dose that keeps control; consider stepping down to an ICS alone. Use a spacer if hand-breath coordination is difficult (re-titrate after starting a spacer). Elderly: no adjustment.

src.q: Once control of asthma is achieved with the lowest strength of Flutiform inhaler administered twice daily treatment should be reviewed and consideration given as to whether patients should be stepped down to an inhaled corticosteroid alone.
Use of a spacer device with Flutiform inhaler is recommended in patients who find it difficult to synchronise aerosol actuation with inspiration of breath.
Re-titration to the lowest effective dose should always follow the introduction of a spacer device.
There is no need to adjust the dose in elderly patients.

items.t: 125/5: not for children under 12 years. 250/10: not for anyone under 18. No strength is recommended under 5 years. A 50/5 strength (same SmPC) is licensed from 5 years.

src.q: Flutiform inhaler 125 microgram/5 microgram per actuation should not be used in this young age group.
Flutiform inhaler 250 microgram/10 microgram per actuation should not be used in adolescents or children.
Flutiform inhaler in any strength is not recommended for use in children less than 5 years of age
Flutiform 50 microgram / 5 microgram inhaler is indicated in adults, adolescents and children aged 5 years and above.

items.t: Monitor height in children on prolonged inhaled corticosteroid.

src.q: It is recommended that the height of children receiving prolonged treatment with inhaled corticosteroids is regularly monitored.

items.t: Not for acute symptoms (use a fast-acting reliever); not the first treatment for asthma; do not start during an exacerbation; do not stop abruptly (down-titrate under supervision).

src.q: Flutiform inhaler should not be used to treat acute asthma symptoms for which a fast and short-acting bronchodilator is required.
Flutiform inhaler should not be used as the first treatment for asthma.
Treatment with Flutiform inhaler should not be stopped abruptly in patients with asthma due to risk of exacerbation.

items.t: Use with caution in thyrotoxicosis, phaeochromocytoma, diabetes, uncorrected hypokalaemia, HOCM, idiopathic subvalvular aortic stenosis, severe hypertension, aneurysm or other severe cardiovascular disorders (ischaemic heart disease, arrhythmias, severe heart failure), and in existing QTc prolongation.

src.q: Flutiform inhaler should be used with caution in patients with thyrotoxicosis, phaeochromocytoma, diabetes mellitus, uncorrected hypokalaemia or patients predisposed to low levels of serum potassium, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, idiopathic subvalvular aortic stenosis
severe hypertension, aneurysm or other severe cardiovascular disorders, such as ischaemic heart disease, cardiac arrhythmias or severe heart failure
Caution must be observed when treating patients with existing prolongation of the QTc interval.

items.t: Hypokalaemia: particular caution in unstable or acute severe asthma; monitor serum potassium then. Consider extra blood sugar checks in diabetes.

src.q: It is recommended that serum potassium levels are monitored during these circumstances.
As for all β2 agonists, additional blood sugar controls should be considered in diabetic patients.

items.t: Adrenal suppression with prolonged high doses (rarely at 500 to under 1000 micrograms fluticasone): consider extra systemic corticosteroid in stress or elective surgery.

src.q: Prolonged treatment of patients with high doses of inhaled corticosteroids may result in adrenal suppression and acute adrenal crisis.
Additional systemic corticosteroid treatment should be considered during periods of stress or elective surgery.

items.t: Caution in pulmonary or quiescent tuberculosis and fungal, viral or other airway infections. A spacer may increase systemic absorption.

src.q: should be administered with caution in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis, quiescent tuberculosis or patients with fungal, viral or other infections of the airway
Use of a spacer device may lead to a possible increase in pulmonary deposition and a potential increase in systemic absorption and systemic adverse events.

items.t: Contains sodium cromoglicate as an excipient: hypersensitivity has been reported with inhaled cromoglicate. Refer to an ophthalmologist if blurred vision.

src.q: Hypersensitivity reactions have been reported in patients using inhaled sodium cromoglicate as an active ingredient.
If a patient presents with symptoms such as blurred vision or other visual disturbances, the patient should be considered for referral to an ophthalmologist

items.t: CYP3A inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir, cobicistat, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole): avoid unless benefit outweighs risk; if used, monitor for systemic corticosteroid side-effects.

src.q: Co-treatment with CYP3A inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir, atazanavir, clarithromycin, indinavir, itraconazole, nelfinavir, saquinavir, ketoconazole, telithromycin, cobicistat) is expected to increase the risk of systemic side-effects.
The combination should be avoided unless the benefit outweighs the increased risk of systemic corticosteroid side-effects

items.t: Beta-blockers (including eye drops): patients with asthma should not normally receive them; if no alternative, a cardioselective beta-blocker with caution.

src.q: Therefore, patients with asthma should not normally be treated with β blockers and this includes β blockers used as eye drops for treatment of glaucoma.
cardioselective β blockers could be considered, although they should be administered with caution

items.t: Loop and thiazide diuretics: caution (ECG changes/hypokalaemia can be acutely worsened). Xanthines and glucocorticoids add to hypokalaemia.

src.q: caution is advised in the co-administration of a β agonist with non-potassium sparing diuretics
Xanthine derivates and glucocorticosteroids may add to a possible hypokalaemic effect of the β agonists.

items.t: Caution with tricyclic antidepressants, MAO inhibitors (and for 2 weeks after stopping them) and other QTc-prolonging drugs (antipsychotics, quinidine, disopyramide, procainamide, antihistamines); caution with other adrenergic drugs by any route.

src.q: Formoterol fumarate, as with other β2 agonists, should be administered with caution to patients being treated with tricyclic antidepressants or monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and during the immediate two week period following their discontinuation
or other drugs known to prolong the QTc interval such as antipsychotics (including phenothiazines), quinidine, disopyramide, procainamide, and antihistamines

items.t: No data in renal impairment; monitor regularly and titrate to the lowest effective dose.

items.t: SmPC: limited data; not recommended in pregnancy, consider only if benefit to the mother outweighs any risk to the fetus, at the lowest effective dose. In labour, restrict to patients in whom benefit outweighs risk.

items.t: BUMPS: inhaled corticosteroids should be continued in pregnancy; no evidence they harm the baby. ICS/LABA inhalers are standard asthma treatment; do not stop asthma treatment because of pregnancy unless advised.
